Done.

## What I changed

**`internal/shell/shell.go`** — Added a length guard at the top of `Run`:

```go
if len(command) == 0 {
    log.Warn("no command to run, skipping")
    return nil
}
```

This prevents the panic from indexing `command[0]` when a pipe entry has no command. It returns `nil` (no error) and uses the project's existing `log.Warn` convention. Nothing else in the function was touched — environment setup, output writers, dir handling, and the error path are unchanged.

**`internal/shell/shell_test.go`** — Added an `empty command` subtest alongside the existing subtests, using testify `require` and the project's `testctx.New()` helper.

## Evidence

- `go build ./...` → exit 0
- `go vet ./internal/shell/` → clean
- `go test ./internal/shell/ -run TestRunCommand -v` → 5 subtests pass, including the new `TestRunCommand/empty_command`
- Grep confirmed `log.Warn` is already the project's warning-logging convention

The `golangci-lint` binary is not installed in this environment, so lint was verified via `go vet` only; the diff is a small guard using existing imports and conventions.

No upstream project sources were consulted.
